text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA
- Yugoslav Justice Minister Zoran Knezevic says there is no legal or other reason to change Yugoslavia's constitution and that insisting on changes could have unforseeable consequences.
- Presidents of opposition Democratic Party (DS) and Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) invited OSCE observers to Belgrade to look into the pre-election situation in Serbia.
- Yugoslavia's constitution does not allow extradition of war criminals, says Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic.

- The second Serb-Kosovo Albanian meeting on education in Kosovo will be held in Pristina or Rome, said Abdul Rama a member of the working group for implementation of the agreement on the normalisation of education in the province.
- Students might resume protest walks on June 17 because of the government decision to raise university fees in the next school year.
- The Serbian teachers' trade union will call its members to strike from the first day of the next school year if the government does not pay wages at agreed intervals.
- Bosnian Serb republic expects Greek telecommunications OTE to participate in the financing of its PTT system and that deal signed with Serbia's PTT is a stepping stone to this.
- Serbian trade minister Srdjan Nikolic to be appointed deputy general manager of Serbian electricity company EPS.
POLITIKA

- Yugoslav-Croatian commissions to meet this week to discuss implementation of agreement on normalisation of relations; the return of Serb refugees and settlement of their property issues will be priority on the agenda.
- Yugoslav businessmen invited to present Yugoslavia's economy in Belgium in December.

- European railway financing company Eurofima granted another ten million Swiss franc credit to Yugoslav railways; funds are expected to arrive at the end of the month and be used for purchase of spare parts and second-hand carriages.
- Socialist Party of Serbia municipal boards throughout Serbia express support for the candidacy of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic for the federal presidency.
BORBA
- Serbian Development Fund will finance projects of strategic interest for the development of the economy.
DNEVNI TELEGRAF
- The distribution of wages in the country resembles a quasi-Stalinist method of exhausting people, says president of the Yugoslav Association of Trade Unions Dragan Radulovic.
- We are planning to harmonise the stands of the federal units with the federal government on taking decisive measures against gray economy, says Yugoslav domestic sales minister Milorad Miskovic.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA

- There is a possibility for Montgenegrin power company Elektroprivreda Crne Gore to participate in the economic recovery of the Serb entity in Bosnia, prime minister Milo Djukanovic told a visiting Bosnian Serb delegation.
- Montenegrin deputy parliament speaker Zoran Zizic is opposed to changes of the federal constitution which he says could jeopardise the equality of the republics.

- The Montenegrin opposition called for live TV coverage of Wednesday's session of the ruling DPS main board which is to discuss proposed changes to the federal constitution and candidacy of Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic as federal president.

- "If (Serbian president Slobodan) Milosevic is elected as the federal president Montenegro will become Serbia's colony" says head of People's party Novak Kilibarda. -- Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
